newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MOTOR RACING-SAFETY CAR OUT AT START OF ARGENTINE G.P..
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SAFETY CAR OUT AT START OF ARGENTINE G.P..

text.p: The third successive first corner accident caused the introduction of a safety car on the opening lap of Sunday's Argentine Grand Prix.
Double world champion Michael Schumacher's Ferrari touched Brazilian Rubens Barrichello's Stewart, sending it into a spin and leaving debris all over the circuit.
As race favourite Canadian Jacques Villeneuve and his Williams' team-mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany led the way, the organisers sent out the safety car to slow the field.
They remained in slow single file for four laps before the track was cleared and the race resumed at normal speed with Villeneuve in front.
Barrichello had some repairs done to his car and was able to restart but Briton David Coulthard in a McLaren was forced out along with Schumacher. No one was injured.
